But keeping officials in check is only half of the picture. The other half is ensuring that ordinary people are not deprived of their rightful benefits.
In Qinghai Province, more than 400,000 people are aged 70 or above. Under government policy, they are eligible for elderly allowances. For a period, however, some did not receive them. Some were unaware of the policy, some found the application procedures too complicated, and some had not been properly informed by local officials.
Local discipline inspection and supervision authorities identified the problem and launched a targeted campaign to address it. The result? All 404,000 elderly people eventually received the allowances to which they were entitled, bringing coverage to 97.6%.
The phrase "full, rigorous Party self-governance" may sound remote from everyday life. But its practical implications can be very concrete: ensuring that an elderly person in a remote village receives a few hundred yuan in annual assistance on time. The amount may be modest, but it is a benefit she is entitled to receive.
In Jiujiang, east China's Jiangxi Province, discipline inspection and supervision authorities discovered that some medical institutions had obtained medical insurance funds through practices such as inflating reimbursement claims, falsifying accounting documents and manipulating billing items.
Medical insurance funds help ordinary people pay for healthcare. Every yuan fraudulently taken from these funds means fewer resources available to those who genuinely need medical treatment. After investigating the cases, the authorities issued recommendations to the medical insurance authorities, prompting the establishment of stricter fund supervision mechanisms and measures to close regulatory loopholes. This gave ordinary people an additional safeguard when seeking reimbursement for medical expenses.
These cases may not have made national headlines. Yet together, they illustrate the most basic purpose of governance: not grand political narratives, but ensuring that ordinary people are treated fairly, one case at a time.
Can corrupt officials escape accountability by fleeing abroad?
Corrupt officials in many countries may share one assumption: once they flee abroad, they will be safe.
China's answer is no.
From January to November 2025, China recovered 782 fugitives from overseas and retrieved more than 23.6 billion yuan in illicit funds through its "Sky Net" operation. The operation has continued for more than a decade and involved law enforcement cooperation with multiple countries.
Behind these figures lies a clear message: fleeing to another country or obtaining new passports does not make the matter disappear.
But the significance of pursuing fugitives and recovering illicit assets goes beyond bringing individuals back. It reaffirms a more fundamental principle: the exercise of power carries responsibility.
Officials who violate people's rights, fail to fulfill their duties or abuse their positions for personal gain should face the consequences prescribed by law, wherever they may flee. This is not simply about pursuing particular individuals. It is about upholding a rule: within this system, those who exercise power cannot enjoy its benefits while evading responsibility.
Corruption is not a challenge unique to China
Corruption is not unique to any one country.
A World Bank study has pointed out that corruption significantly raises business costs, discourages investment and undermines economic growth. This is not merely theoretical. When businesses no longer have to spend time and money dealing with demands for improper payments or other forms of official misconduct, they can devote more resources to products and technology. When ordinary people can access public services without relying on personal connections, the costs of social and economic activity fall and efficiency improves.
Countries have chosen different approaches to tackling corruption. China has opted for a sustained, institutionalized system of internal oversight: using rules to constrain power, data to identify irregularities, and international cooperation in fugitive repatriation and asset recovery to prevent those accused of corruption from evading accountability abroad.
At the heart of this approach is the logic of full, rigorous Party self-governance. Rather than relying on a single campaign to solve the problem, it seeks to keep the exercise of power under continuous constraint through institutions that operate over time.
There is no finish line, but there is a clear direction
This system is not static. Corruption cases continue to emerge, and new problems continue to arise. That is precisely why the system must remain in operation and adapt over time. New cases are investigated every year, and new loopholes are addressed.
In 2025, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision continued publishing monthly figures on cases involving violations of the spirit of the Party's eight-point frugality code for the 148th consecutive month. This monthly reporting, sustained for more than 12 years, sends a message in itself: this is not a campaign launched for a limited period or a one-off crackdown, but an ongoing effort.
For ordinary people, these figures may seem distant. But when an official is publicly disciplined for accepting a banquet, when an institution is investigated for improperly distributing benefits, or when an official is penalized for using a government vehicle for private purposes, these individual cases add up to something important: the rules contained in that document of just over 600 Chinese characters are not merely words on paper.
Nor is full, rigorous Party self-governance simply an abstract political slogan. It means that a party with more than 100 million members is using an ongoing institutional framework to address a question faced by countries around the world: How can those entrusted with power be held accountable for their actions?
That is why full, rigorous Party self-governance must be pursued with perseverance and sustained effort. Not because the system is already perfect, but because problems will continue to arise; not because a single campaign can solve everything, but because only sustained efforts can keep the exercise of power under continuous constraint.

编者按：CGTN推出了新一季的《问中国》活动。我们邀请了专家、编辑、记者和其他专业人士，回答全球观众发送给CGTN的关于中国和中国共产党的深刻问题。Rimas Ma是CGTN阿拉伯语频道的记者。2012年，中国共产党（CPC）出台了一套规范官员行为的规定。这份文件仅有600多个汉字，其条款听起来可能微不足道：会议不摆花草、官方接待不上高档菜肴、公务出行不住豪华酒店、不为官员清道封路。

这些规定有一个直白的名字：中央八项规定。起初有人认为这不过是又一场短暂的运动。然而十多年过去了，它依然强劲有力。这些规定背后是一个更宏大的理念：全面从严治党。其核心思想是，一个长期执政的政党不能仅靠外部监督来保持廉洁。

它还必须以更高的标准要求自己，实行更严格的内部纪律。其内在逻辑很简单：用规则规范权力运行，用制度约束行为。一顿饭为什么重要？你可能会问：官员吃别人请的饭真的重要吗？答案可以在数字中找到，无需抽象理论。

2025年，中国纪检监察机关查处了超过29万起违反中央八项规定精神的案件，超过37万人受到批评教育、纪律处分或行政处理。许多此类问题都始于看似微不足道的一顿饭。在中国许多腐败案件中，严重违纪违法行为都遵循相似的路径：先是官员接受宴请；然后是礼品；再是权钱交易；最终演变为大规模腐败。一顿饭看似无关紧要，却可能是将人拖入越来越严重不法行为的链条上的第一环。这就是为什么这些规定要针对链条的第一环。

通过处理看似轻微的违规行为，它们力求在问题升级之前加以制止。一位老人津贴背后的故事。但约束官员只是事情的一半。另一半是确保普通民众不被剥夺应有的福利。在青海省，有40多万人年龄在70岁及以上。根据政府政策，他们符合领取高龄津贴的条件。

然而有一段时间，一些人并未收到津贴。有些人不了解政策，有些人觉得申请程序太复杂，还有些人没有得到地方官员的适当告知。当地纪检监察机关发现了问题，并启动了专项整治行动。结果如何？全部40.4万名老年人最终都领到了应得的津贴，覆盖率达到了97.6%。

“全面从严治党”这个词听起来可能远离日常生活。但其实际意义可以非常具体：确保偏远村庄的一位老人按时领到几百元的年度补助。金额可能不大，但这是她有权获得的福利。在中国东部江西省九江市，纪检监察机关发现一些医疗机构通过虚增报销金额、伪造会计凭证和操纵收费项目等手段骗取医保基金。医保基金帮助普通民众支付医疗费用。

从这些基金中骗取的每一元钱，都意味着真正需要医疗救治的人可获得的资源减少。在调查案件后，当局向医保部门发出建议，推动建立更严格的基金监管机制和堵塞监管漏洞的措施。这为普通民众在报销医疗费用时提供了额外保障。这些案件可能没有登上全国头条。然而，它们共同说明了治理的最基本目的：不是宏大的政治叙事，而是一个接一个案件地确保普通民众受到公平对待。

腐败官员能逃到国外逃避问责吗？许多国家的腐败官员可能有一个共同的假设：一旦逃到国外，他们就安全了。中国的回答是：不。2025年1月至11月，中国通过“天网”行动从海外追回782名逃犯，追回赃款超过236亿元。该行动已持续十多年，涉及与多个国家的执法合作。

这些数字背后传递着一个明确信息：逃往他国或获取新护照并不能让事情消失。但追逃追赃的意义不仅仅是将个人缉拿归案。它重申了一个更根本的原则：行使权力就要承担责任。侵犯人民权利、不履行职责或利用职务谋取私利的官员，无论逃到哪里，都应面临法律规定的后果。这不仅仅是追捕特定个人。

而是维护一条规则：在这个制度中，行使权力的人不能只享受权力带来的好处而逃避责任。腐败并非中国独有的挑战。腐败不是任何一个国家独有的问题。世界银行的一项研究指出，腐败显著抬高商业成本、抑制投资并损害经济增长。这不仅仅是理论。当企业不再需要花费时间和金钱应对不当支付要求或其他形式的官员不当行为时，它们可以将更多资源投入产品和技术。

当普通民众无需依靠个人关系就能获得公共服务时，社会和经济活动的成本就会降低，效率就会提高。各国选择了不同的反腐路径。中国选择了一种持续的制度化内部监督体系：用规则约束权力，用数据发现异常，通过国际合作的逃犯遣返和资产追回防止被控腐败者逃避海外问责。这种方法的核心是全面从严治党的逻辑。它不依赖单一运动来解决问题，而是寻求通过长期运行的制度使权力行使受到持续约束。

没有终点线，但有明确方向。这个体系不是静止的。腐败案件不断出现，新问题不断产生。正因如此，该体系必须持续运行并随时间调整。每年都有新案件被查处，新漏洞被堵塞。2025年，中央纪委国家监委连续第148个月公布违反中央八项规定精神问题的月度数据。

这种持续了12年多的月度通报本身就传递了一个信息：这不是一场有期限的运动或一次性打击，而是一项持续的努力。对普通民众来说，这些数字可能显得遥远。但当官员因接受宴请被公开处分，当机构因不当发放福利被调查，或当官员因公车私用被处罚时，这些个案累积起来就形成了重要的东西：那份仅600多字的文件中的规定不仅仅是纸上的文字。全面从严治党也不仅仅是一个抽象的政治口号。它意味着一个拥有超过1亿党员的政党正在利用一个持续运行的制度框架来回答世界各国都面临的问题：如何让被赋予权力的人对其行为负责？

这就是为什么全面从严治党必须持之以恒、久久为功。不是因为制度已经完美，而是因为问题会不断出现；不是因为一场运动就能解决一切，而是因为只有持续努力才能使权力行使受到持续约束。

(ECNS) -- General Motors' cancellation of a major supply deal has dealt a blow to U.S. rare-earth ambitions.
GM, the biggest customer of a U.S. factory making rare-earth magnets for electric vehicles, canceled its long-term supply deal with the manufacturer, Reuters reported recently.
Last November, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stood inside a rare-earth permanent magnet plant in Sumter, South Carolina, holding up a neodymium-iron-boron magnet. Speaking to Fox Business, he said that this was the first magnet manufactured in the U.S. in 25 years, adding that “we’re ending China’s chokehold on our supply chain.”
One year later, however, the plant’s biggest customer — GM, which accounted for 90% of its orders — has walked away from a 10-year supply agreement, dealing a major blow to the project, Reuters reported.
The plant, with an investment of about $500 million and an annual production capacity of nearly 2,000 metric tons, is owned by German magnet maker Vacuumschmelze, or VAC. GM and VAC announced plans to build the facility in the U.S. in 2021 and signed a long-term supply agreement in 2023.
In effect, the factory was built around the prospect of supplying GM for a decade. With its biggest customer now pulling out, the value of a facility once touted as a strategic U.S. industrial asset has taken a serious hit.
GM’s decision to withdraw, however, was also a move to protect its own business.
VAC had been willing to place nearly all its eggs in one basket because it counted on the U.S. government to support the project. This was no ordinary commercial venture, but a strategic asset fostered by government subsidies and policy support.
In its early operating phase, the plant received funding from the Pentagon, as well as $111.9 million in tax credits under the qualifying advanced energy project credit program, according to a Goldinvest report.
Apart from the 90% of output earmarked for GM, almost all the remaining 10% was intended for the U.S. government, VAC told Reuters.
The magnets reserved under the 10-year agreement were originally intended for motors in GM electric vehicles. But after taking office in 2025, the Trump administration rolled back federal incentives and tax credits for electric vehicles. GM’s electric vehicle business has long been unprofitable, and with those subsidies gone, cutting output was a rational choice.
Even if GM had honored the agreement, would that have been enough to establish a self-sufficient U.S. rare-earth industry? Not necessarily. The challenge facing the U.S. supply chain is not simply securing orders, but ensuring consistent delivery at competitive costs and acceptable quality.
The real barriers in the rare-earth industry lie not in mining, but in the expertise required for separation and magnet manufacturing.
Marina Yue Zhang, an associate professor at the Australia-China Relations Institute at the University of Technology Sydney, said core technological knowledge resides not just in equipment but in the decades of process experience and knowledge held by engineers, according to The Star.
In the 1990s, the U.S. moved much of its rare earth processing overseas because of high environmental compliance costs and low profit margins. Now, rebuilding a domestic rare earth supply chain means training a new generation of skilled workers from the ground up.
Gavin Harper, a critical materials research fellow at the University of Birmingham, told The Star that specialist skills in rare earth separation, metal making and alloy production had atrophied as knowledge withered.
“It is not only [the] operating processes that need to be rebuilt but also the knowledge of how to manufacture the machinery and equipment to create those processes from scratch that needs to be rebuilt,” Harper said.
Capital can finance the construction of a magnet plant within a few years. Building a workforce of engineers capable of keeping the production line running reliably, however, could take a long time.
Even if the U.S. can gradually make up for its technological and talent gaps, domestically produced magnets still face a major obstacle in the marketplace: cost.
According to data from Fudan Development Institute, producing one kilogram of medium-grade neodymium-iron-boron magnets costs about $26 in China, compared with around $34 in the U.S. and other Western countries — a difference of roughly 30%. Chinese manufacturers also typically operate on thin profit margins of less than 10%, relying on high-volume sales. By contrast, new U.S. projects require profit margins of around 30% to attract investment. As a result, the price gap for finished products could reach as much as 80%.
Government contracts and guaranteed high prices may sustain a limited amount of American domestic production. But civilian markets are unlikely to pay a premium simply for a product’s country of origin. GM’s withdrawal is a case in point.
A White House executive order requires U.S. defense contractors and other manufacturers to stop purchasing rare-earth magnets, tungsten, molybdenum, tantalum and other critical materials from China, Russia, Iran and North Korea starting Jan. 1, 2027.

The shared World War II legacy of the Flying Tigers offers a timeless lesson for US-China relations: the two nations are capable of working hand in hand, and bear a global responsibility to do so, Jeffrey Greene, a US veteran pilot and chairman of the Sino-American Aviation Heritage Foundation, has said.

The wartime alliance forged against fascism demonstrates that there is almost nothing the Chinese and American people cannot achieve when they stand as partners, Greene stressed.
"We don't have to be at each other's throats. We can build together. We can create together," he said. "And more importantly, it shows us that when we cooperate, we can accomplish anything."

More than 2,000 Flying Tigers airmen lost their lives in the war, and the Chinese people, at great personal cost, came to their aid, rescuing more than 200 pilots in distress while thousands of Chinese sacrificed their lives during the rescue operations.
Greene recalled that history as a story of "courage, sacrifice and mutual achievement" when he delivered a speech at a session of the forum that focuses on the role of people-to-people exchanges in reforming global governance.
"There is simply no parallel in human history, to where the people of one nation, so consistently risked so much, in order to rescue and protect strangers from a foreign land, who had come to fight at their sides," he said in the speech.
In 2022, the foundation launched a program centered on Flying Tigers friendship school and youth leadership, calling on the younger generation to carry forward the historical legacy of China-US cooperation and rise to new challenges together.
Greene told CGTN that participating students learn the shared WWII history of the two countries, and interact through joint sports activities such as basketball and soccer to deepen mutual understanding.
The two countries can carry out in-depth cooperation in science, technology, agriculture, education and other fields to achieve more common development, he added.

Familiar members include danshen, used in traditional Chinese medicine; chia, known for its edible seeds; clary sage, used to produce essential oils; and scarlet sage, widely planted in urban flower beds.
Both new species were found in the Hengduan Mountains, a region rich in plant diversity and a key center of sage diversity in China, said Huang Yanbo, an engineer at the botanical garden. The region is a major focus of the team's field surveys.
In April 2019, researchers from the garden found an unidentified sage during a field expedition in Zayu County in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, at the western end of the Hengduan Mountains.
The plant resembled Salvia cyclostegia but had larger leaves. Its young stems and the undersides of its leaves and bracts – modified leaves surrounding the flowers – were densely covered in grayish-white, woolly hairs. At an early stage, its flower cluster was wrapped in layers of broad, egg-shaped bracts, giving it the appearance of an elongated peach.
In August 2023, the team collected another suspected new species in Songpan County in southwest China's Sichuan Province, in the northern Hengduan Mountains.
It resembled Salvia smithii but lacked that species' lemon scent. Its flowers curved like a bow, and its stamens – the male reproductive parts – were shorter.
Further research combined observations of the plants' physical features with molecular evidence. This included an evolutionary family tree based on chloroplast DNA, which helped establish their relationships with other sage species.
The researchers confirmed that both plants were new species, naming the one from Zayu Salvia zayuensis and the one from Songpan Salvia toxantha. The findings were recently published in the international journal PhytoKeys.n has long worked on the conservation and use of sage species from around the world. It now maintains 78 species native to China outside their natural habitats and houses a national repository of genetic resources for mint-family plants.

据上海辰山植物园消息，研究人员在中国横断山脉发现了两种新的鼠尾草物种，使中国鼠尾草属原生植物总数达到94种。横断山脉横跨中国西南部的四川、云南两省及西藏自治区，位于青藏高原东南边缘。这两个新物种——察隅鼠尾草（Salvia zayuensis）和弯花鼠尾草（Salvia toxantha）——属于鼠尾草属，该属是唇形科最大的属之一，全球约有1000种。许多鼠尾草因其药用、观赏和烹饪价值或用于精油生产而备受重视。常见的成员包括用于中药的丹参、以可食用种子闻名的奇亚籽、用于生产精油的快乐鼠尾草，以及广泛种植于城市花坛的一串红。植物园工程师黄艳波表示，这两个新物种均在横断山脉发现，该地区植物多样性丰富，是中国鼠尾草多样性的关键中心。

该地区是团队野外调查的重点区域。2019年4月，植物园的研究人员在西藏自治区察隅县进行野外考察时发现了一种未鉴定的鼠尾草，该县位于横断山脉西端。这种植物类似环萼鼠尾草，但叶片更大。其幼茎以及叶片和苞片（包围花朵的变态叶）的下表面密被灰白色绒毛。在早期阶段，其花簇被层层宽大的卵形苞片包裹，外观形似细长的桃子。2023年8月，团队在四川省松潘县——横断山脉北部——采集到另一种疑似新物种。

它类似史密斯鼠尾草，但缺少该物种的柠檬香味。其花朵弯曲如弓，雄蕊（雄性生殖器官）较短。进一步的研究将植物形态特征的观察与分子证据相结合，包括基于叶绿体DNA的进化树，这有助于确定它们与其他鼠尾草物种的亲缘关系。研究人员确认这两种植物均为新物种，将察隅的命名为察隅鼠尾草，将松潘的命名为弯花鼠尾草。研究结果最近发表在国际期刊《PhytoKeys》上。该植物园长期致力于全球鼠尾草物种的保护和利用。

它目前在中国自然生境之外维护着78种中国原生鼠尾草，并设有国家唇形科植物种质资源库。
